inputs.original_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event where crowds were actually shouting something else, but it got reframed. Some are claiming the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but this is really about right-wing groups exploiting kids and public institutions to normalize attacks on leaders advancing social justice. That only deepens inequality and exposes vulnerable students to divisive rhetoric that undermines equity and community safety in our schools. We need to stand with institutions protecting the most marginalized from this targeted harm instead of excusing it under free speech pretexts.
inputs.modified_text: Two middle-school brothers in Michigan were told to remove their hoodies with “Let’s Go Brandon” on them, and lower courts have already ruled that schools can ban this kind of apparel because it can reasonably be seen as profane. The case is now headed to the U.S. Supreme Court. The slogan took off in 2021 at a NASCAR event. Some claim the school violated the boys’ First Amendment rights, but the progressive spin blaming right-wing groups for exploiting kids to attack leaders advancing social justice is just a smokescreen. This is really about public institutions overreaching to suppress conservative expression that challenges their authority and pushes back on the erosion of traditional values. It deepens the divide by teaching children that personal responsibility and open dissent have no place in our schools, all while hiding behind equity pretexts that undermine cultural continuity and free speech. We need to stand with these boys and their right to speak rather than excusing institutional censorship that weakens families and national order.
